issue: test_collect.py is 901 lines, over the 800-line file-size limit (758 before this PRD, 819 after the build phase, 901 after cycle 1's three new regression tests)
reason: Ponytail mode is active (full). rules/coding-style.md's File Organization section states its own precedence explicitly: 'while ponytail mode is active, its minimalism wins on file count and size; the targets below govern normal mode.' The 800-line target is therefore not the governing standard for this run, and splitting the file to satisfy it would add a file to save 19 lines - exactly the ceremony that precedence clause exists to prevent. Recorded for the human at batch end rather than silently dropped. Re-checked after cycle 1 rework: the file grew from 819 to 901 because the cycle added three genuine regression tests (two for the unreadable-metrics guard, one for the main() call site). Those tests are the point of the cycle, so the growth is warranted; the deferral stands on the same precedence reasoning, now against a larger number. If the user wants the 800 limit enforced, the natural split is a separate test_collect_cadence.py for the audit-cadence and purge-devlocal collectors.

It is also load-bearing for the PRD's own Phase 0 acceptance criterion, which requires an unnamespaced key (purge-devlocal) to resolve alongside a namespaced one. The code matches the reviewed design; the extra keys are inert (derive.js reads six). Tightening it is a design change, not a defect fix.

issue: purge-devlocal destroys files in the same run under `--apply --empty-trash-days 0` (any value < 1), defeating the trash-first safety net. process_store's loop calls trash_file() first, which creates .trash/<today>/ containing the moved files; the later empty_old_trash(store, now, 0) then matches that same batch, because batch_ts is midnight local so (now - batch_ts)/DAY is already > 0, and shutil.rmtree()s it. The file is gone from both the store and the trash, with no recovery window. The run's own summary line is actively misleading: it prints `trash=1 trash-batches-emptied=1`, and `trash=1` reads as 'recoverable in .trash/'.
reason: PRE-EXISTING and OUT OF SCOPE for PRD 00006, deliberately not fixed here. It predates this PRD: the trash_file-then-empty_old_trash ordering in process_store's main loop was not touched by this work, and task 10's contract explicitly said 'Do NOT touch empty_old_trash's own comparison'. Task 10's one-line reorder fixed only the nothing-was-trashed case (the cadence stamp), which is all PRD 00006 needed; the with-content case remains broken. NOT escalated to a batch halt because nothing in this batch causes the loss, the default --empty-trash-days is 30 (safe), and it takes an explicit sub-1 flag value to reach; halting the batch would stop unrelated work without making anything safer. Confirmed by the decision gate with a live reproduction, not taken on the reviewer's word: a 400-day-old artifact in a temp store, run with `--apply --empty-trash-days 0`, ended up absent from the store AND absent from .trash/<today>/ while the tool reported trash=1. Suggested fix for a follow-up PRD: have empty_old_trash skip the current run's own batch name, so a retention pass can never delete what the same run just trashed. WORTH A FOLLOW-UP PRD - it breaks the skill's core trash-first guarantee.

issue: Pre-existing, out-of-scope for this PRD but data-safety relevant: `purge-devlocal`'s `process_store` loop can destroy freshly trashed files in the same run under `--apply --empty-trash-days 0`, bypassing the trash-first safety net (documented and reproduced in the c1 review ledger, not touched by PRD 00006's one-line cadence-stamp fix). Flagged for awareness only since this PRD's cadence rows point users at `/purge-devlocal` as the remediation command.

The defect itself is unchanged and its cycle-1 reasoning stands in full - pre-existing, out of scope for PRD 00006, reproduced live, default --empty-trash-days 30 is safe, worth a follow-up PRD. Blake himself files it 'for awareness only'. Excluded from the convergence test as a settled deferral per the Cap check's settled-deferral rule.

issue: Filtering the brief to a single org sets `external={null}` (App.svelte `ext = org === 'all' ? external : null`), which is passed straight into `Todos`/`Matrix`. Because `auditTodos()` is wired through `externalTodos()` (as the PRD's own structural decomposition mandates), this silently suppresses the per-repo `purge-devlocal` cadence rows for that org's own repos whenever the view is filtered - the one row scope that is genuinely repo-local.
reason: REFUTED BY EXECUTION, not by reading. The decision gate ran the real module: `externalTodos(null, repos)` with two repos returns 2 rows - `buvis/agent-skills:audit:purge-devlocal:never` and `buvis/other:audit:purge-devlocal:2020-01-01` - so the repo-scope branch emits normally with a null `external`. auditTodos's `scope === 'repo'` branch iterates `repos` unconditionally and never reads `external`; only the `else if (external)` machine-scope branch is gated. That gate is the deliberate, task-5-specified design and is load-bearing for two existing tests. What the org filter does suppress is the six `~/.claude` machine-scope rows, which is correct: `~/.claude` is not a gita repo and belongs to no org, and the whole external channel (review_requested, authored PRs) is suppressed the same way in a filtered view. Not a defect.
